Registrations, pinned declarations, defaults and reproducible consumer boundaries

**REQ-126 C02 complete — 26 October 2026:** [Function/options reconciliation](FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles 30 entries/74 function surfaces with explicit supported boundaries and 14 follow-up groups. Release build and all 21,798 solution tests pass; all 3,148 catalog examples pass separately. The 195 added profile observations include 118 matching controls, two unmet controls for the new `atomic-type-annotation(())` defect, and 75 diagnostics. Eleven closure workpackages remain; C03 is next. C02 closes review scope, not AC-01–04 or the retained defects. Skip fixes, Braid and extension work remain deferred. Original receipts and frozen gates are preserved; no engine/version/release change. **REQ-126 C01 complete — 26 October 2026:** [Current inventory and ownership record](FUNCTION-INVENTORY-REFRESH.md) refreshes 316 names against published 1.26.3 and pinned current draft b4723ff5: 119 registered 4.0-only names (70 non-constructors, 49 focus constructors), plus 197 existing names. The [machine-readable comparison](audit-signature-contracts.json) records live registrations, coarse dispatch kinds, optional sequence-type metadata, keyword names/default expressions and pinned function declarations. Source evidence: [FunctionLibrary](../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs), [FunctionSignature](../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Functions/XPathFunction.cs), and [QT4CG F&O catalog e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). Current review pins do not reconstruct historical adoption. ## How to read the comparison 37 families have no keyword metadata; 47 have names matching a pinned signature; four have different names. Within the 68-name scope, 31 have keyword metadata and 37 lack it. Metadata absence is distinct from absence of positional registration. The char case demonstrates that distinction; behavior is not inferred for every absent-metadata family. Exact registrations are implementation dispatch entries. Pinned call arities are ranges derived from the declared required/default arguments, not a claim that every named reference/lookup is available. fn:replace is the only selected range difference: the draft permits two arguments, while exact registrations are 3 and 4. Its positional/reference two-argument calls refuse XPST0017 and lookup returns zero; its keyword default form returns 42 for INV-42 with pattern INV-. Default comparison normalizes only quoted string literals and empty-map spellings. Matching text does not prove evaluation timing, focus capture or complete omission/default-on-empty behavior. jkey, jvalue and node-name have a required parameter in keyword metadata where the pinned declaration supplies `.`. Their registered zero-argument forms are present; this metadata difference alone does not prove those calls fail. Coarse dispatch kinds are not precise draft sequence types or evidence of enforced coercion. The 148 lookup fixtures verify exact registration availability and default 3.1 visibility; experimental scan is also checked against frozen visibility. They do not invoke every overload with valid data. The **39 behavior fixtures** provide separate value/error evidence for selected defaults, keywords and hash options. The [detailed consumer README](examples/signature-contracts/README.md) publishes complete invoice input/output and runnable files. operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md.text:
Numeric literals and digit separators

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

**Public1.23.7 - 23 October2026:** EQName bracket parsing, inline-record signature gates and numeric separator boundaries are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.7-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Hexadecimal/binary integer literals and underscore separators** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S3. Lowercase `0x` and `0b` introduce integer literals. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0. Current comparison: [immutable grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), productions NumericLiteral, HexIntegerLiteral, BinaryIntegerLiteral, DecimalLiteral, DoubleLiteral, Digits, HexDigits and BinaryDigits. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4. ## 2. Intent Make a bit mask or a large threshold readable in source code while retaining the numeric value and ordinary arithmetic semantics. ## 3. Also Known As Based integer literals; digit separators. `0xFF` is an integer, not an xs:hexBinary byte value. Binary literals are numbers, not xs:base64Binary values. Uppercase hex digits are accepted; uppercase prefixes `0X` and `0B` are refused. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1 use decimal `255` instead of `0xFF`, `4` instead of `0b0100`, and `1000` instead of `1_000`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) keep the same telemetry report algorithm; only the constants change. Literals do not introduce a new runtime numeric type or relax input casting. ## 5. Motivation A telemetry feed stores flags and counts as decimal attributes. A report selects readings with bit 4 set and count at least 1000. The mask is easier to inspect in binary and the threshold easier to read with grouping. The [complete task](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) includes normal, empty, reordered and invalid inputs and exact output. ## 6. Language Alignment The prefixes resemble C-family source literals; the exact XPath grammar governs the boundaries. Repeated internal underscores such as `1__000` and `0xFF__FF` are valid under the pinned draft. Each nonempty digit group starts and ends in a digit: `1._2`, `1.2_` and `1e_2` are invalid. A sign is a unary operator, not part of the integer token. Source separators do not extend the XML Schema lexical forms accepted by xs:integer: `xs:integer('1_000')` and `xs:integer('0xFF')` still fail FORG0001. ## 7. Applicability Use these constants in authored XPath/XSLT 4.0 expressions. Keep external decimal attributes in their declared lexical format, and select a 3.0/3.1-compatible spelling when generating an older stylesheet. This entry verifies ordinary Legacy-host effective3.0/4.0 stylesheets, not every package, XQuery or host override context. ## 8. Structure ```xpath 0xFF + 0b1_000 + 1_000 ``` The sum is1263. `1_2.3__4` is decimal12.34; `1_2.5e+0_2` is double1250. A decimal point may have no following digits (`1_2.`), and a decimal may omit its integer part (`.1_2`). If a fraction/exponent group is present, its separators cannot be at an edge. ## 9. Participants [XPathLexer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Lexer/XPathLexer.cs) scans version-sensitive numeric tokens. [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) removes separators and computes based integer values. The public XPath31Expression/CompileOptions surface selects the compatibility level. No new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations In the report the binary constant and hexadecimal zero form the mask; idiv/mod test the flag arithmetically. A separated threshold filters counts. xsl:for-each preserves input order, and sum builds the total from parsed decimal attribute values. The literals do not implement bitwise operators or alter data conversion. ## 11. Consequences The supplied checks cover integer/decimal/double identity, a value above Int64 range, negative unary application, numeric map/array lookup keys, valid internal repeated separators, malformed groups, wrong radix digits and version refusals. Bosak uses bounded .NET numeric representations; one above-Int64 example does not certify arbitrary-precision integer/decimal support. Other numeric adjacency, Unicode digit and overflow behavior is outside this bounded correction. No performance improvement is claimed. ## 12. Implementation **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies 4.0 radix/separator syntax and lower-profile refusal; Above-Int64 integer literals versus generic constructors/casts; Delivered floating thresholds, unsigned truncation and preserved integer identity. **Boundary:** A decimal-backed wide literal does not establish arbitrary precision or a matching generic constructor range. Generic wide xs:integer casts still narrow; .NET decimal precision remains bounded. Ownership: T01, T02. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Fifty new catalog cases use the existing public CatalogExampleTests execution path. Initial38 probes produced30 passes and8 failures: malformed fractional/exponent underscore groups were accepted. Source1.23.7 rejects those groups only in the 4.0 lexer path. Thirty-four dedicated API cases cover those eight shapes in all four compatibility levels and valid-group controls in both4.0 profiles. Expected outcomes were not weakened. [Audit and retained evidence](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md). ## 13. Sample Code The complete [4.0 report](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) reads [normal.xml](../examples/numeric-literals/normal.xml): readings A(flags5,count1500), B(flags2,count900). It emits `A:ready|B:hold|ready=1;total=2400`, matching the3.0 baseline. Empty input emits `ready=0;total=0`; reordering changes row order; invalid count `oops` raises FORG0001. [Task and all expectations](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) describe every instruction and input assumption. ## 14. Performance Notes Digit separators are removed during compilation; based integers are accumulated in the parser. These facts are implementation descriptions, not allocation or timing measurements. Report arithmetic and numeric conversion still run per reading. No benchmark or asymptotic improvement over decimal constants is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `numeric-literals-hex`, `numeric-literals-binary`, `numeric-literals-fraction`, `numeric-literals-exponent`, `numeric-literals-beyond-long`, `numeric-literals-invalid-13` and `numeric-literals-report-4-normal`, enumerated with all fifty cases in [the audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [NumericLiteralBoundaryTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/NumericLiteralBoundaryTests.cs) methods Compile_InvalidDigitGroup_ThrowsXpst0003 and Evaluate_ValidDigitGroups_ReturnExpectedValues independently cover the correction. Existing [VersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) methods Evaluate_HexBinaryLiterals_XPath40Mode_Work, Evaluate_UnderscoreSeparators_XPath40Mode_Work and Evaluate_HexBinaryLiterals_31Mode_ThrowXpst0003 remain relevant. Feature-specific qt4 assignment is explicitly unassigned in this slice; running the unchanged global gate does not establish individual production coverage or promote a set. ## 16. Related Features [String templates](string-templates.md), [keyword arguments](keyword-arguments.md), [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). The [grammar matrix](../GRAMMAR-COVERAGE-MATRIX.json) retains remaining host/declaration coverage. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC-03 remain partial.

Focus-function syntax and pipeline focus

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

## 1. Name and Classification **Focus-function syntax** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S4. `fn { E }` and `function { E }` omit the signature and take one `item()*` argument, bound as the whole context value. `fn($x) { E }` abbreviates an ordinary explicit-signature inline function; it is not a focus function. This entry is distinct from the [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md). Delivery: [PR #87](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/87), immutable `ec79355936a29ac70eeea3ae47e4c4e2ee00d813`; that revision already contains the named focus-function tests. Current review: [immutable draft expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), sections `id-inline-func`, `id-focus-functions`, `id-pipeline-operator`, and [InlineFunctionExpr grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml). Upstream master was refreshed on 22 October 2026. This is a current comparison pin, not recovery of a historically adopted specification revision. Source 1.23.5 remains unpublished; public 1.23.4 already contains this bounded syntax. ## 2. Intent Write a callback whose argument supplies its context value, and distinguish per-item processing from whole-sequence reduction. ## 3. Also Known As A focus function is an inline function without an explicit signature. Both `fn { ... }` and `function { ... }` are supplied forms. The keyword abbreviation `fn($x) { ... }` still has an explicit parameter list. A zero-argument constructor such as `xs:integer()` is a different feature. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, write `function($line as element()) { xs:decimal($line/@qty) * xs:decimal($line/@unit) }`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-4.xsl) produce the same order-line report. A parameterized 3.1 function does not implicitly bind its parameter as the focus; references use `$line` explicitly. ## 5. Motivation An order feed contains line quantity and unit amount. The report computes one amount per line, preserves source line order, then reports the count and total over all amounts. A focus callback keeps the attribute calculation readable; the pipeline makes the whole-sequence summary distinct from the mapping stage. [The complete task and fixtures](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) state assumptions, exact input/output and failure behavior. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath focus, not ambient JavaScript `this` or an implicit item-by-item lambda. The callback receives a sequence as a single argument and sets position/size to 1/1, even for an empty or multiple-item argument. `=!>` calls its target per input item; `->` evaluates its right expression once with the complete left value as context. The 3.1 `=>` arrow inserts a first function argument; it does not establish the pipeline context. Similar results for a unary example do not make these operators interchangeable. ## 7. Applicability Use a focus function for an attribute-oriented callback or a whole-value operation when its context contract is clear. Use explicit parameters when argument names/types improve clarity or caller position must be passed explicitly. In the report each amount callback receives exactly one line node. Empty input makes no mapping calls; the summary pipeline still runs once with an empty value. ## 8. Structure ```xpath fn { concat(count(.), ':', position(), ':', last()) }((9,8)) ``` This returns `2:1:1`. The runnable [whole-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/whole-focus.xpath) returns `2:1:1` (count:position:size), and [empty-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/empty-focus.xpath) returns `0:1:1`. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser.ParseInlineFunction](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) lowers an omitted signature into a single synthetic parameter plus a PipelineExprNode. [IrLowerer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs) and [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) execute the existing function/focus path. Public callers use XPath31Expression/CompileOptions or ordinary XSLT stylesheets; no new API is introduced. ## 10. Collaborations The report's `$amount` focus function reads the supplied line; `$format` uses the explicit `fn(...)` abbreviation and typed named arguments; the per-item label callback captures those variables. Mapping creates line labels and amounts. The pipeline consumes the amounts as one value for count and sum. Caller focus is restored after inner calls/pipelines, as verified by named probes. ## 11. Consequences A callback argument containing two items is not two calls. A callback invoked from a simple map sees its own position/size 1/1, not the caller's 1/N, 2/N positions. An axis such as `@qty` requires an appropriate node context; the implicit signature alone does not validate the report's line schema. Wrong lexical decimals raise FORG0001 in both report versions. Values are formatted to two display decimals, without claiming a general accounting model. ## 12. Implementation Thirty new manifest cases use the existing CatalogExampleTests public execution path: 18 focused values/grammar/focus probes, four explicit 3.1 refusals and eight complete stylesheet reports. Sixteen successful XPath cases also assert a 3.1 refusal; two compatible forms retain baseline results. No engine, test runner, compatibility level or gate is changed. The reports use the default Legacy host with effective stylesheet versions 3.0/4.0, not an exhaustive host/module/package matrix. ## 13. Sample Code Input: ``. Both complete stylesheets yield `BOLT=25.00|NUT=10.00|FREE=0.00|lines=3;total=35.00`. Empty input yields `lines=0;total=0.00`; reordered input changes label order while retaining count/total. An invalid quantity `oops` raises FORG0001. [Full examples](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) include every fixture, expected result, context and runnable file. ## 14. Performance Notes The report makes a bounded number of passes over N lines/amounts and emits O(N) labels. Function items and sequence materialization may allocate; no speed or memory advantage over the baseline is claimed. Use the benchmark harness for measured claims. Focus functions do not make the report streaming or parallel. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable evidence under the owner-approved AC-03 policy: `focus-syntax-report-3-normal`, `focus-syntax-report-4-normal`, their empty/reordered/invalid counterparts, and the `focus-syntax-*` probes in [the manifest](../examples/cases.json), executed by [CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs). All 30 case IDs and receipt hashes are recorded in [the slice audit](../FOCUS-FUNCTION-SYNTAX.json). Named existing tests in [VersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs): `Compile_FocusFunction_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_SpecExamples`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_BindsArgumentAsWholeContextValue`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_AfterMappingArrow`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_WrongArityThrows`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_SetsFixedFocusPositionOneSizeOne`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_FocusRestoredAfterEvaluation`. **No feature-specific qt4 gated-set assignment is made here**; named engine tests and runnable public examples are the explicit evidence. This does not assert that upstream lacks broader tests or claim whole-set conformance. The policy amendment does not automatically close acceptance of this or other entries. ## 16. Related Features [Pipeline](pipeline-operator.md), [mapping arrow](mapping-arrow.md), [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md), [keyword arguments](keyword-arguments.md), [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). Record casts/coercion/updates remain the next separate D3 scope.

experimental/fn-scan.md.text:
fn:scan

Catalog entry — Functions · Experimental

## 1. Name and Classification **`fn:scan`** — **Experimental** (ships only at the `XPath40Experimental` level; static XPST0017 at both `XPath31` *and* frozen `XPath40`). Spec: F&O 4.0 §2.5.15, added by qt4cg Issue 2823 / PR 2824 (31 July 2026). Landed: REQ-123 S1 (1.1.0 track), level-plumbing slice 2026-10-09. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [F&O 4.0: fn:scan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-scan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. Draft evolution: [QT4CG PR #2824](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/2824) records the scan proposal referenced by the adoption dossier. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #98](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/98), [immutable mainline revision `bd18e42f`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/bd18e42f33b5e69817f059f6429f4b08e639a5a3) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Return every intermediate accumulator of a left fold as a **sequence of single-member arrays**: `fn:scan($input, $init, $action)` yields `[$init]`, then `[$action($acc, $item, $pos)]` for each input item — N input items produce N+1 arrays. There is no additional outer array. ## 3. Also Known As "Prefix scan", "running fold". **Do not implement** `scan-left` / `scan-right`: those names never existed in the accepted draft — the pair was consolidated into the single left-fold `fn:scan` before stabilization (see [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) for the sibling rename story). ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes hand-threaded accumulation of intermediate states in 3.1. The [complete stock-ledger baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) uses `fold-left` and `array:append`; the [experimental case](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath) uses `fn:scan`. Both display `100,120,85,95` for an opening stock of 100 units and movements of +20, -35, and +10. | Before (3.1) | After (4.0-Exp) | |---|---| | `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` | ## 5. Motivation Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison. ## 6. Language Alignment Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback. ## 7. Applicability Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state. Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move. ## 8. Structure ``` fn:scan(input as item()*, init as item()*, action as fn(*)) as array(*)* ``` ## 9. Participants - `FunctionLibrary` — experimental-only signature template (`IsXPath40ExperimentalOnly`), invisible to `fn:function-lookup` / dynamic dispatch below the experimental level. - `EvaluationContext.IsXPath40Experimental` — runtime level flag. - Version gate (`XPath31Expression`) — static XPST0017 in call form *and* named-function-ref form at both lower levels. ## 10. Collaborations - The **experimental level plumbing** (REQ-123 S1) is the collaboration that matters: `fn:scan` was the first function gated exclusively to `XPath40Experimental`, and it established the template every later experimental addition follows (dedicated signature templates, lookup invisibility, call+ref static errors). - Destructuring `let` ([destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md)) is the natural consumer of each emitted single-member array's shape in surrounding code. ## 11. Consequences Benefits: direct expression of all intermediate states; the callback position parameter enables position-aware accumulations. Retaining the history requires storage for its states; no constant-memory guarantee is implied. Liabilities: **experimental-tier semantics may change as the draft moves** — the N+1 / single-member-array shape is precisely the kind of detail a WG review adjusts. Pin your usage to a Bosak version and re-run the qt4tests `fn-scan` set (if promoted by then) on upgrades. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles N+1 accumulator states retain single-member array boundaries; Empty input retains the initial state; Position-aware callback; Experimental-only availability. **Boundaries:** No frozen-profile adoption or constant-memory guarantee; generic function coercion beyond verified callbacks is not certified. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs` (experimental signature + implementation), `src/Bosak.XPath.Api/XPath31Expression.cs` (experimental-aware static gate), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (`IsXPath40Experimental`). Version gate: XPST0017 at `XPath31` **and** `XPath40`; legal only at `XPath40Experimental`. Unit evidence: experimental-level tests in `Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests` (see REQ-123 S1). ## 13. Sample Code Practical case: [stock ledger](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath). The [empty-movement case](../examples/fn-scan/edge.xpath) returns only the opening balance, displayed as `100`. Both cases require `XPath40Experimental`; the [earlier baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) runs at `XPath31`. ~~~xquery fn:scan((1, 2, 3), 0, fn($acc, $it) { $acc + $it }) (: → [0], [1], [3], [6] — every running total, init first :) fn:scan((), "start", fn($acc, $it) { $acc || $it }) (: → ["start"] — empty input yields just the init :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Implementation expectation: one callback per input item and one wrapper array per retained state. Accumulator size can dominate storage and callback cost. No measured comparison against the 3.1 array-append baseline is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses Published examples: `fn-scan-main`, `fn-scan-edge`, `fn-scan-before` in `CatalogExampleTests`. The successful experimental cases also verify refusal at both lower compatibility levels. This is example evidence, separate from gate status. qt4tests set `fn-scan` is promoted into `GatedSets` in [ConformanceRunner40](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). The 1.1.0 gate run records 11 experimental-level passes and zero gated failures. Gate membership does not move the function into the frozen compatibility tier; its successful examples still require `XPath40Experimental`. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Evaluate_Scan_XPath40Experimental_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-scan`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) — the sibling "consolidated/renamed before stabilization" story. - [destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md) — frozen-tier contrast from the same delivery wave. - [method-call-operator.md](../operators-and-syntax/method-call-operator.md) — another post-June-2026 deferred surface. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold).*
